landing.packetsTitle: pick the chores — errandly does the rest
landing.packetsText: Add a task once: the system decides whose turn it is and reminds them in time.
landing.cloudText: Chores aren’t about who loves cleanliness more. They’re about agreements. Errandly takes over the boring part: it tracks everyone’s workload, rotates tasks and skips whoever went home for the weekend. All that’s left is to do your part.

features.groupText: Create a group for your flat or dorm room and send your flatmates a link.
features.tasksText: One-off or recurring, with a difficulty from 1 to 5 and a due date.
features.fairText: A task goes to whoever has the lowest workload over 4 weeks. Ties take turns.
features.calendarText: Your tasks show up in Google Calendar with a reminder.

landing.ctaText: Free, for groups of 2 to 10 people.

tips: Mark a task as done with one tap on the circle on the left. By accident? The notification has an “Undo” button.
Going home for the weekend? Add an absence in the “Group” section — you won’t get tasks on those days.
Click a task to quickly change the assignee, edit it or open the details.
Difficulty 1 is two minutes, 5 is a deep clean. An honest estimate means a fair split.
Connect Google Calendar in the settings — tasks will show up there with a reminder.
Want to swap a task? Talk to the admin — they can change the assignee manually.
“Statistics” shows who did how much. Transparency is the best cure for arguments.
The split counts the workload over 4 weeks. Whoever did more gets fewer new tasks.
If everyone has the same workload, the task goes to whoever hasn’t done it the longest.
In the calendar each assignee has their own colour — you can see at once who carries the week.
A striped bar in the calendar means that person is away that day.
An admin can add a task right from the calendar — with the “+” button next to a day.
Recurring tasks are created 4 weeks ahead and keep topping themselves up.
Deleting a recurring task? You can remove just one occurrence or the whole series.
The chips on the banner are clickable: “1 overdue →” scrolls straight to that task.
The bell at the top collects all group events: new tasks, new members, overdue ones.
Don’t want an email about every little thing? Each type of email notification can be turned off in the settings.
Change the theme in the settings — “Sakura”, “Pixel” or “Sunset”.
Animations distracting? There’s a “Reduce motion” switch in the settings.
The admin sees tasks without an assignee — an “unassigned” chip appears on the banner.
An invitation is valid for 7 days. Expired? Just create a new link.
Leaving the group while you’re the only admin? Hand over the rights to another member first.
Washing the dishes right after dinner is difficulty 1. Three days later it’s a full 5.
The trash won’t take itself out. But Errandly will at least remind you whose turn it is.
The best task is a finished task. The second best is one rescheduled in time.
Hang a trash reminder by the door — and let the calendar take care of the rest.
